- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply downward correction of 3–8% in subsequent days, especially if sentiment turns neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.2) and model forecasts are high, reduce forecast by 5–10% to align with mean reversion tendency.
- Model often underestimates prices in early horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; add 1–3% to forecast for first 3–5 days if sentiment is rising.
- If sentiment is flat or mildly positive (0.0–0.3) and model is consistently below true outcome, apply a 2–5% upward bias correction for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is negative and true outcome is rising, model often misses the rebound; adjust forecast upward by 3–7% if sentiment turns positive within next 3 days.
- Model tends to lag sentiment shifts by 2–4 days; if sentiment changes direction, adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect sentiment shift.
- For long-term (15+ day) forecasts, model often overestimates; apply 5–10% downward correction if sentiment is weak or negative.
